taxonomic_note: Accepted at species rank. A later illegitimate use of the name by L.f. is not treated as a separate learner taxon.
look_here_first: Start with leaf shape and petiole before flower color: broad triangular to ovate-deltoid serrate leaves on conspicuous petioles. Then confirm the verticillate flowering axis and long bilabiate corolla.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Opposite broad triangular to ovate-deltoid serrate leaves on conspicuous petioles, 4-angled stems, repeated flower verticils, persistent ribbed calyx, and long bilabiate corolla.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County native list, Travis County Balcones Canyonlands records, and UT Williamson County treatment; no county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual to short-lived perennial/subshrub tendency; usually branched, often 0.5–1 m tall.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite decussate, simple, petiolate; blades triangular or ovate to deltoid with serrate margins.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Interrupted series of verticils/cymes along a terminal axis.
morphology_keys.calyx: Persistent, ribbed and enlarging around developing nutlets.
morphology_keys.floral_detail: Long bilateral corolla; typically red in local material but color is secondary to leaf and inflorescence structure.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Cedar sage may also be red but has a low shaded-juniper habitat and different leaf architecture. Azure sage has narrow linear leaves and a much taller open flowering axis.
